channel.title: youHide — blog
channel.description: Notes from the homelab and from production — infrastructure, Go and Rust, and the things that broke on the way. Posts are bilingual EN / PT-BR; feed summaries are in English.

item.title: A tap that pulls: a Homebrew tap nothing pushes to
item.description: The usual way to maintain a Homebrew tap is for each project to commit its own formula into it, which means storing a token with write access to the tap in every project that ships through it. My tap now pulls instead: an hourly workflow reads each project's latest GitHub release and regenerates the formulas and the README from one TOML table per tool. No project knows the tap exists, no project needs a write token, and the platform a formula offers is decided by which asset keys the table has.

item.title: The same store, the same keys: a pass-compatible password manager in Rust
item.description: hidePass is a password manager in Rust that does not own its format: it reads and writes the pass store you already have, with the same gpg keys and the same git commits, and CI cross-checks it against the real pass on every push. One-time codes, EFF diceware passphrases, named fields and a store audit are built in rather than installed — and copied secrets are marked concealed and transient, so clipboard managers decline to record them.

item.title: Nothing above it to restart it: writing an init for Linux in Rust
item.description: PID 1 is the first program the kernel starts and the only process with no supervisor above it: if it exits, the kernel panics. oxinit is a service manager and PID 1 for Linux written in Rust — no panic, unsafe quarantined in one file and enforced by the build, one epoll loop on one thread with no async runtime, TOML units where requires and after are separate statements, and a non-goals list that does most of the design work.

item.title: The engine was not a choice: eight years in the games industry
item.description: Eight years in the games industry, 2017 to 2025, spent on the infrastructure side of studios where the engine was Unity and nobody in the room had chosen it. The version nobody upgrades, logic that cannot be tested outside the editor, an iteration loop set by the tool, and a licence that was never mine to control — and what I ask of a tool now.

item.title: Nothing decays in secret: building Greenvale
item.description: Greenvale is a real-time farming simulation in Rust where soil depletes, metal rusts and pests evolve — and every loss is traceable to a cause. What happens when a platform engineer designs a game: map overlays as dashboards, the post-harvest report as a postmortem, and determinism as test infrastructure.

item.title: Deleting the build step: this site is hand-written HTML again
item.description: Two pages of content were being served by a static site generator, a vendored theme pinned to a 2019 commit and an FTP deploy action pinned to @master. What came out, what went in, and why zero external requests is worth keeping.
